posts.originalContent: **Anthropic's Lawsuit Against the U.S. Department of Defense** Anthropic filed a lawsuit against the Pentagon on March 9, 2026, challenging its designation as a "supply chain risk" after the company refused to allow its AI tools to be used in autonomous weapons or government surveillance, escalating an ongoing feud. The dispute has drawn support from AI leaders and highlights potential $5 billion losses for Anthropic, with allegations that the DoD used its tools despite the ban.[[1]](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/03/09/technology/anthropic-defense-artificial-intelligence-lawsuit.html)[[2]](https://www.wired.com/story/anthropic-claims-business-is-in-peril-due-to-supply-chain-risk-designation) **Governance angle**: Exposes breakdowns in institutional coordination between AI firms enforcing safety guardrails and military/government entities, questioning the legitimacy of unilateral risk labels and the need for clearer cross-sector agreements on permissible AI uses. **Source URL**: https://www.nytimes.com/2026/03/09/technology/anthropic-defense-artificial-intelligence-lawsuit.html

posts.originalContent: **Pro-Human AI Declaration Launch** A new coalition launched the Pro-Human AI Declaration in March 2026, uniting experts from organizations like Future of Life Institute and Center for Humane Technology, along with figures such as Stuart Russell and Yoshua Bengio. It outlines five principles prioritizing human control, avoiding power concentration, protecting human experience, ensuring agency/liberty, and holding AI companies accountable via liability and independent standards.[[3]](https://humanstatement.org/) **Governance angle**: Builds cross-organization legitimacy through broad coalitions and public-backed principles (e.g., polls favoring superintelligence bans), pushing for mandatory oversight, transparency, and democratic processes beyond self-regulation to coordinate safe AI development. **Source URL**: https://humanstatement.org/
